result.rationale: The user wants a new video made, and the inventory is empty (no videos, images or audio). That rules out edit_existing and create_full, so this is create_minimal with graphics-led scenes. The goal, audience, platform, duration and tone are stated. treatment.logline: A calm, silent, typographic explainer that turns a messy booking-email thread into one tidy calendar confirmation, ending on a free 14-day trial invitation for Slotly.
treatment.hook: 0–4s: On a clean off-white 16:9 canvas, email-style bubbles bounce back and forth ("Does Tuesday work?", "Can we do Thursday?", "Actually, Friday?") and stack until the frame feels crowded. No logo and no title card.
treatment.tone: Calm, clear, modern. Soft neutral palette with one accent colour, smooth eased motion, generous white space and large sans-serif type. There is no voiceover or music, so on-screen text and motion carry the story.

beats.beat: HOOK – Back-and-forth: motion-graphic booking bubbles ping-pong and pile up (C03).
beats.purpose: Show the audience's pain concretely in the first frame, with no logo or slow title.

beats.beat: PROBLEM – The bubbles tangle. Text appears: "Booking shouldn't take this many emails." The text sits inside the title-safe area.
beats.purpose: Make the problem felt and state the benefit as a viewpoint. It makes no numeric or time-saving claim.

beats.beat: SOLUTION – The tangle clears into a simple calendar graphic with open time slots. A cursor picks one slot, which turns into a confirmed booking. Text: "Share your open times. Your client picks one." The interface is a stylised concept illustration, not a real screenshot (C04).
beats.purpose: Explain in one visual what the product does. It is shown as a concept because there is no product footage.

beats.beat: FIT – Text only, with no third-party logos: "Works with Google Calendar and Outlook." The two names slide in beside the calendar graphic (C02).
beats.purpose: Give an approved proof point that lowers the barrier to trying the app.

beats.beat: CTA – The calendar clears to the typeset word "Slotly" (a text wordmark, since no logo file exists) with a button-style graphic below. Text: "Start your free 14-day trial." The text holds static for the last 2 seconds so it can be read (C01).
beats.purpose: Give one clear action tied to the sign-up goal, and show the brand name long enough to register.

uses.rationale: Punchy hook with no overlay: the crowded bubble thread cuts straight to the tangle in S02. Hard cut is the default and keeps pace tight.
The headline should appear after the slow push-in has tightened on the tangle, then hold. Entrance ends at 1.6s, well inside the 60% limit (2.4s of 4s), leaving about 2.4s to read.
The storyboard asks for a crossfade out of the problem into the solution, a calm mood shift as the tangle clears. 0.8s is under the half-scene limit of 2s.

The line explaining the product appears just after the calendar graphic forms, so the text and the cursor action support each other. One dominant text motion in the scene. Entrance ends at 1.3s of 5s.
Storyboard specifies a cut from the solution to the compatibility proof point. The cut is quick and keeps the pace up.
A short, quick entrance for the approved compatibility line as the names slide in. It ends at 0.9s, inside the 60% limit (1.8s of 3s), so the line can be read.
The storyboard specifies a crossfade into the closing scene. 0.6s is under the half-scene limit of 1.5s.

The closing card holds the CTA text static for the final 2 seconds, as the brief requires. The light background matches the off-white canvas. The recipe is used once, and a 2s hold fits a 4s scene. I did not add dip-to-black because S05 is the final scene and has no following scene to transition into. Fading the last frame would also cut into the 2s static hold.
